content: If you miss a dose of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions or ask your pharmacist for specific guidance. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Clindamycin, commonly sold under the brand name Cleocin, is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is administered by injection into a vein or muscle, typically 2 to 4 times daily, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. Antibiotics work best when the medication level in your body is maintained at a constant level. Continue using this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, a metallic or unpleasant taste in the mouth (if injected into a vein), or pain at the injection site (if injected into a muscle). Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood/mucus in your stool, contact your doctor immediately, as these may indicate a serious intestinal condition caused by Clostridium difficile bacteria. This condition can occur weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Before using clindamycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to lincomycin, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as benzyl alcohol) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Clindamycin may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. Additionally, this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., kidney or liver function tests) to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to determine the best course of action. Always store this medication as directed by the product instructions or your pharmacist.
